segments.flavor: the station ID, landing like the house signature
segments.text:
Michael: Midnight Jazz. Everything worth saying gets quieter after one in the morning.
Michael: So does everything worth playing. Here it comes.

segments.flavor: the station ID, the street outside the window
segments.text:
Michael: The streetlights are doing their best. The coffee gave up an hour ago.
Michael: Midnight Jazz. Stay exactly where you are, and let the music work.

segments.flavor: the station ID, one line and a locked door
segments.text: Michael: Midnight Jazz. Noir hours only. The door locked an hour ago. Play on.

segments.flavor: the station ID, with Sarah refusing to let it land clean
segments.text:
Sarah: Midnight Jazz. Velvet, low light, and a host who pretends he is fine.
Michael: Mm. I am fine.
Sarah: Heh. Sure. Play the horns.

segments.flavor: a slow noir observation about the city at night that turns into a dry punchline
segments.text:
Michael: Every parked car on this block points the same direction tonight. Nobody planned that.
Michael: The city agrees on one thing a night, and it chose parking. More music.

segments.flavor: Sarah teases Michael about a habit; he loses gracefully; back-announce {STREAM} on the way out
segments.text:
Sarah: You stirred that coffee again. It is black. There has never been anything to stir.
Michael: It settles my thinking.
Sarah: Heh. It settles nothing. You just like the sound the spoon makes.
Michael: ...I like the sound the spoon makes. Take us back into the horns.

segments.flavor: a 'last call' style toast to everyone still awake, with one unexpected twist
segments.text:
Michael: Last call, quietly. To everyone still awake on purpose, and everyone awake by accident.
Michael: The second group is bigger, better dressed, and owns all the better stories. Horns, go.

segments.flavor: George stumbles in with barstool wisdom that is accidentally profound; Michael and Sarah react
segments.text:
George: I always take the last stool. Nobody sits past you. Nobody walks behind you.
Michael: That is either wisdom or a security habit.
George: At my age they are the same thing.
Sarah: Hahaha. Michael, write that on a napkin before he forgets it.
Michael: He will not forget it. He has said it nine times tonight.
George: Ninth time is when it starts working. Put the music back on.

segments.flavor: a slow noir observation about the city at night that turns into a dry punchline
segments.text:
Michael: Two blocks over, the bakery light comes on. The only honest window on the street.
Michael: Everybody else is faking it until sunrise. Heh. So are we. Roll it.

segments.flavor: Sarah teases Michael about a habit; he loses gracefully; back-announce {STREAM} on the way out
segments.text:
Sarah: You are tapping again. Three beats, every time, like a waltz nobody asked for.
Michael: I do not tap.
Sarah: You tapped through the whole last number. The desk knows the tune by heart.
Michael: ...the desk and I have an arrangement.
Sarah: Mm-hm. You lost this one. Say goodnight to the desk.
Michael: Goodnight, desk. Back into the music, where the tapping is legal.

segments.flavor: a 'last call' style toast to everyone still awake, with one unexpected twist
segments.text:
Michael: Last call. The toast goes out to everybody who never quite got around to the business of going home.
Michael: I am raising the melted ice in a chipped glass, and somehow it still counts. Back to the music.

segments.flavor: George stumbles in with barstool wisdom that is accidentally profound; Michael and Sarah react
segments.text:
George: A jukebox is honest. You pay, you pick, and then you live with it.
Michael: That is the whole arrangement, yes.
George: Life is a jukebox where somebody else already paid.
Sarah: [gentle] Oh, that one landed. George, do you hear yourself?
George: Rarely. That is how I keep saying good things.
Michael: Heh. He is not wrong.
Sarah: He is never wrong after midnight. That is the rule.
Michael: Then let the rule stand. Horns, take it from here.

segments.flavor: a slow noir observation about the city at night that turns into a dry punchline
segments.text:
Michael: There is a traffic light on an empty corner, working its full routine for absolutely nobody tonight.
Michael: Green, amber, red, patient as a saint. We should all work like that. Cue the piano.

segments.flavor: Sarah teases Michael about a habit; he loses gracefully; back-announce {STREAM} on the way out
segments.text:
Sarah: You said let it breathe again. That is four times tonight. I counted.
Michael: Music needs room.
Sarah: Wine needs room. Music needs a needle and somebody who stops talking.
Michael: ...that is a fair hit.
Sarah: I have more. You also say mm when you agree, which is not a word.
Michael: It is a word in this building.
Sarah: Heh. It is a noise with a union card.
Michael: I concede. Let it brea— let the horns have it.

segments.flavor: a 'last call' style toast to everyone still awake, with one unexpected twist
segments.text:
Michael: Last call at the counter. Raise whatever is in reach.
Sarah: To the people still awake.
Michael: To the boiler in the basement, actually. It has not quit in forty years.
Sarah: [surprised] Oh. That is where you were going with this.
Michael: It works nights, it makes a terrible noise, and nobody thanks it.
Sarah: So it is you, with pipes. To the boiler, and back to the bandstand.

segments.flavor: George stumbles in with barstool wisdom that is accidentally profound; Michael and Sarah react
segments.text:
George: Every story worth telling starts the same way. Somebody left, and somebody stayed.
Michael: And which one tells the story?
George: The one who stayed. The other one is busy.
Sarah: Hahaha. George, that is the meanest true thing I have heard all week.
Michael: Mm. Mean and accurate overlap more than people like to admit.
Sarah: They overlap constantly. That is why you two get along so well.
Michael: We get along because he lets me finish a sentence.
George: I let you start one. Finishing has always been your own business.
Sarah: [laugh] Oh, he got you. He got you clean.
Michael: He did. Hold the stool, George. Music, hold the room.

segments.flavor: a slow noir observation about the city at night that turns into a dry punchline
segments.text:
Michael: The last bus went past with every light on and nobody inside it.
Michael: Somewhere a schedule is being honored for its own sake. Respect. Roll the tape.

segments.flavor: Sarah teases Michael about a habit; he loses gracefully; back-announce {STREAM} on the way out
segments.text:
Sarah: That pen has been behind your ear for three hours. It has never written anything.
Michael: It is ready if something happens.
Sarah: Michael, nothing happens here. That is the entire appeal of the place.
Michael: Something could.
Sarah: Heh. If something happens, you will describe it beautifully and forget to write it down.
Michael: ...that has occurred before.
Sarah: It occurs nightly. You narrate. I keep the notes. The pen keeps your ear warm.
Michael: The pen has seniority.
Sarah: The pen has tenure. It will outlast both of us and never file a word.
Michael: Fine. You win, as usual.
Sarah: I always do. Now let the music write something down for once.

segments.flavor: a 'last call' style toast to everyone still awake, with one unexpected twist
segments.text:
Michael: Last call, and the glass goes up for anybody who planned to quit something tonight and did not.
Michael: They are not brave, only slow. In this house that earns the same medal. Music, please.

segments.flavor: George stumbles in with barstool wisdom that is accidentally profound; Michael and Sarah react
segments.text:
George: Two cubes. Always two. One is stingy and three is an apology.
Michael: An apology for what?
George: For whatever a man is about to say after the fourth drink.
Sarah: [chuckle] He has a system. Michael, he has a whole system.
Michael: He has a philosophy with a garnish.
Sarah: Mm. Two cubes. Noted forever. Let the horns pour the next one.

segments.flavor: a slow noir observation about the city at night that turns into a dry punchline
segments.text:
Michael: The hotel sign down the block lost a letter. It has read OTEL for years.
Sarah: And nobody fixed it.
Michael: Nobody fixed it. At some point a broken sign becomes the name of the place.
Sarah: That is true of signs. Is it true of people?
Michael: ...ask me again at four in the morning.
Sarah: Heh. I will set an alarm and everything.
Michael: Set two. I will gracefully dodge the first one.
Sarah: You always do, and I always let you. Take it away, horns.

segments.flavor: Sarah teases Michael about a habit; he loses gracefully; back-announce {STREAM} on the way out
segments.text:
Sarah: You have not looked at the clock once tonight. Not once.
Michael: I know what time it is.
Sarah: You know what song it is. Those are different sciences.
Michael: Third ballad means quarter past. Fourth means the coffee is a crime.
Sarah: [laugh] That is not a clock. That is a superstition with a playlist.
Michael: It has never been wrong.
Sarah: It has never been checked. There is a difference, and I am enjoying it.
Michael: ...you are enjoying it visibly.
Sarah: I am. Look up, Michael. Tell me the hour. I dare you.
Michael: Mm. Somewhere between the slow one and the slower one.
Sarah: Hahaha. Correct, unfortunately. Give the slower one some room.

segments.flavor: a 'last call' style toast to everyone still awake, with one unexpected twist
segments.text:
Michael: Last call, and the counter is open to the honest.
Sarah: Define honest.
Michael: Anybody who meant to do one thing today and did not do it.
Sarah: Oh, that is everyone. That is the whole room.
Michael: That is the point. To the undone thing. It waited. It will keep waiting.
Sarah: [gentle] To the undone thing. It is very patient.
Michael: Patience is all it has. Mm. It has outlasted better plans than mine.
Sarah: And now the horns, which have never waited for anybody in their lives.

segments.flavor: George stumbles in with barstool wisdom that is accidentally profound; Michael and Sarah react
segments.text:
George: Every coat check has one coat nobody comes back for. Every single one.
Michael: There is one in the closet here. Grey. Been there since before me.
George: That coat is somebody's whole decision. They chose the cold instead.
Sarah: [gasp] Oh. George. That is horrible and I love it.
Michael: It is a little horrible.
Sarah: It is beautiful horrible. There is a difference and he found it.
George: I did not find it. I left a coat like that once, and walked.
Michael: ...ah.
Sarah: [gentle] Oh, George. And it was warm out, I suppose.
Michael: He made a call. The coat made its own.
Sarah: Heh. Let the grey coat hang. Horns, take the room.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for a product only this station would sell
segments.text:
Michael: A word from the counter. The Long Night Curtain. Nine layers of velvet, zero daylight.
Sarah: The Long Night Curtain does not know what day it is and refuses to learn.
Michael: Hang it once. Wake up whenever it feels earned.
Sarah: Users report missing appointments, seasons, and one entire wedding.
Michael: The Long Night Curtain. Daylight is only a rumor. Back to the record.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for the coffee that is really a decision
segments.text:
Michael: Sponsored by Fourth Cup. Roasted at midnight, ground at midnight, brewed with an apology.
Sarah: Fourth Cup is not coffee. It is a decision about tomorrow.
Michael: One cup, and the night opens like a door with no lock.
Sarah: Do not operate a conversation. Do not promise anything before dawn.
Michael: Fourth Cup. The third cup was the polite one.
Sarah: Mm. Pour carefully. Horns, pour freely.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for a turntable with one honest flaw
segments.text:
Michael: The Ambrose Turntable. Solid brass arm, felt mat, and one honest flaw.
Sarah: The Ambrose will not lift the needle. Ever. That is the flaw.
Michael: Side one plays until somebody in the room admits they want it to stop.
Sarah: Nobody admits it. Households have been rearranged around this machine.
Michael: The Ambrose. It waits longer than anybody.
Sarah: Heh. Let it wait. Let the horns go.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for weather that cannot change its mind
segments.text:
Michael: New from the back room, the Wet Street Machine. One sound, recorded perfectly.
Sarah: One sound. Rain on one street. The same street, all night, forever.
Michael: Some nights a person needs weather that cannot change its mind.
Sarah: The Wet Street Machine has no other settings and will not take requests.
Michael: It is honest work. Set it low and let the room get older.
Sarah: [gentle] Mm. And now some weather with a horn section.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for a lamp with strong opinions about seating
segments.text:
Michael: Presenting the Two Foot Lamp. It lights a chair. It lights nothing else.
Sarah: The Two Foot Lamp has been described as unhelpful by three separate electricians.
Michael: The rest of the room goes soft, and the troubles lose the address.
Sarah: Troubles have been known to find it anyway. The lamp is not a lawyer.
Michael: The Two Foot Lamp. Small light, large opinion about where to sit.
Sarah: Sit down. Horns are coming.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for stationery that never mails anything
segments.text:
Michael: From our sponsor, the Unsent Notebook. Good paper, black cover, no address line.
Sarah: The Unsent Notebook has never mailed anything. That is the entire product.
Michael: Write the whole speech. The one with the good ending. Then close the cover.
Sarah: Contents have been read aloud at exactly zero important moments.
Michael: The Unsent Notebook. Say it all. Say it here.
Sarah: And say nothing over the horns. They are up.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for a car service that refuses the fast route
segments.text:
Michael: Tonight's sponsor is Long Way Cars. Same fare, wrong route, on purpose.
Sarah: Long Way Cars will not take the bridge. The bridge is too quick.
Michael: The driver says nothing. The meter runs like a slow song.
Sarah: Long Way Cars is not liable for anything realized in the back seat.
Michael: Some things only arrive at forty miles an hour with the window down.
Sarah: Mm. Window down. Volume up. Go.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for a machine with a very small conscience
segments.text:
Michael: The Kindly Machine answers the phone and keeps only the pleasant calls.
Sarah: Everything else is filed under weather and never mentioned again.
Michael: Sixty seconds of tape. Brass housing. One very small conscience.
Sarah: The Kindly Machine has deleted apologies, confessions, and two job offers.
Michael: It meant well. That is the most any machine can offer.
Sarah: [chuckle] Let it mean well. Let the horns mean more.

segments.flavor: the three o'clock weather for a city that is not on any map
segments.text:
Michael: And now the three o'clock weather, for a city that has never appeared on a map.
Sarah: Conditions at the harbor are wet, which is the harbor's only setting.
Michael: Fog on the low streets. Fog on the high streets. Fog in the elevator.
Sarah: Visibility is one block, which locals consider generous.
Michael: Overnight low is a coat and a half. Tomorrow, the same, warmer in the lie.
Sarah: [chuckle] Warmer in the lie. Put that on the tourism poster.
Michael: They did. Nobody came.
Sarah: Their loss. That is the three o'clock weather, and here is the sound of it.

segments.flavor: the last word, where Sarah hands Michael a word and he defines it
segments.text:
Sarah: Time for the last word. Michael, the word is glimmer.
Michael: Glimmer. Light that is not committed to anything yet.
Sarah: Go on.
Michael: A glimmer is hope with an alibi. It can always say it was passing through.
Sarah: [laugh] Hope with an alibi. He does this nightly and I never see it coming.
Michael: I have had years of practice and very little else to do.
Sarah: Mm. One point to the gentleman at the microphone.
Michael: Keep the point. I will trade it for the next four minutes of piano.
Sarah: Sold. Piano, you are up.

segments.flavor: the case file, a noir case with an extremely dull solution
segments.text:
Michael: Open the case file. A man loses his keys at midnight and calls it fate.
Sarah: It is not fate.
Michael: He retraces the evening. The coat, the counter, the cab, the long walk home.
Sarah: The keys are in the coat.
Michael: The keys are in the coat. They were always in the coat.
Sarah: Case closed in eleven seconds. You took four minutes.
Michael: The four minutes are the case, Sarah. Anybody can find keys.
Sarah: Heh. Not anybody. Some of us have a spare and a system.
Michael: And no story to tell about it.
Sarah: [laugh] Ouch. That is a hit. A clean one, too.
Michael: Mm. The file closes. The music opens.

segments.flavor: the house cocktail, named after a feeling
segments.text:
Sarah: The house cocktail tonight is called The Almost.
Michael: I am afraid to ask what is in it.
Sarah: Rye, one sugar, and the bitters somebody meant to buy and did not.
Michael: So it is short one ingredient.
Sarah: It is short one ingredient. That is why it is called The Almost.
Michael: Heh. Does it work?
Sarah: It works beautifully. Nobody has ever finished one and nobody has ever complained.
Michael: That is the finest review a drink can get.
Sarah: Stir it slow. The horns will handle the rest.

segments.flavor: the long silence, five seconds held for something specific
segments.text:
Michael: It is time for the long silence. Five seconds, and we hold it for something.
Sarah: What are we holding it for?
Michael: Every conversation that ended one sentence too early.
Sarah: [gentle] Oh. That is a very big silence.
Michael: It is. Five seconds will not cover it. We start somewhere.
Sarah: [whisper] Then start counting, and I will not say a word.
Michael: Five. Four. Three. Mm. Close enough.
Sarah: Heh. You never make it to one.
Michael: I never do. Let the piano finish the count.

segments.flavor: the night menu, read aloud although the kitchen is closed
segments.text:
Michael: The kitchen closed hours ago, so here is the night menu, read for its own sake.
Sarah: Nothing on it is available.
Michael: Soup of the day, which was a fine day. Bread, warm at one point.
Sarah: The fish was excellent and is now a memory with bones.
Michael: Dessert is a story the cook tells about a cake in another city.
Sarah: [chuckle] The cake in the other city. It gets better every time.
Michael: It does. Kitchen closed. Menu read. Appetite untouched.
Sarah: Mm. Nobody leaves hungry if the horns are generous.

segments.flavor: the closing line from a novel nobody wrote
segments.text:
Michael: And now the closing line, from a novel nobody wrote and everybody has read.
Sarah: Let us hear it.
Michael: He locked the door, and for the first time the room agreed with him.
Sarah: [sigh] Ohhh. That is good. That is annoyingly good.
Michael: It came to me at the counter and refused to leave.
Sarah: Who published this one?
Michael: Nobody. That is why the ending holds up.
Sarah: Heh. Shelve it carefully. The strings are waiting.

segments.flavor: the second set, the band that plays after everyone goes home
segments.text:
Sarah: Here comes the part where Michael describes the second set again.
Michael: The second set starts when the last customer leaves and the chairs go up.
Sarah: There is no second set. The band goes home.
Michael: The band goes home. The room keeps playing. That is the second set.
Sarah: Michael.
Michael: Radiators on the low end. Ice machine on the two and four.
Sarah: [laugh] The ice machine is not a drummer.
Michael: The ice machine is the most reliable drummer in this city.
Sarah: Mm. It never asks for a solo, I will give it that.
Michael: It never asks for anything. It just keeps time until somebody returns.
Sarah: [gentle] All right. You win this one. Barely.
Michael: Barely is a win. Second set, take over.
